risks.note: The AR states that rapid technological changes may impact product relevance and market competitiveness. In a networking market moving from Wi-Fi 6 to Wi-Fi 6E and early Wi-Fi 7, and to multigig and 100G fiber, a portfolio that lags a generation loses design wins; the Company's mitigation is continuous evaluation of emerging technologies and portfolio enhancement.

The Company relies on global supply chains for electronic components and networking products; supply disruptions, logistics constraints and component shortages may affect procurement and delivery timelines. The MD&A and the Chairman's letter both flag intermittent constraints in semiconductor availability and periodic shortages of critical chipsets affecting procurement cycles, pricing and lead times - a direct constraint on an EMS/ODM whose output depends on imported inputs.

Fluctuations in foreign exchange rates may impact procurement costs and profitability because of the Company's dependence on imported products and components. The AR notes the appreciation of the US Dollar against the Rupee led to higher import costs for component-dependent industries, and foreign exchange outgo during the year was INR 5,958.44 lakhs in actual outflows - a large gross import bill relative to the business, making margins FX-sensitive.
risks.risk: Foreign exchange exposure on imported components

risks.note: Changes in regulations relating to telecommunications, product certifications, customs duties and compliance requirements may impact business operations. The Company's market access depends on TEC certification, ITSAR Proterm certification and Trusted Telecom Portal listing; a change in those regimes or a lapse in certification directly gates sales to telecom service providers.

The networking industry remains highly competitive with participation from both domestic and global players, and the Chairman's letter describes intense competition from multinational brands. The MD&A additionally lists competitive pricing pressures and extended customer procurement cycles as industry-level challenges, which compress realisations for a value-positioned Indian brand.

Smartlink invests its surplus funds in financial instruments such as mutual funds, bonds, non-convertible debentures and other securities, and is thereby exposed to credit risk, market risk and interest rate risk. This is a structural feature of the holding-company balance sheet: a meaningful part of earnings sits outside the operating business and is mark-to-market sensitive.
risks.risk: Treasury / investment portfolio risk on surplus funds

risks.note: Increasing digital connectivity exposes the business to cybersecurity threats that may affect operations, customer confidence and reputation - a compounding exposure for a vendor of networking and connectivity infrastructure, where a security incident in the product line would also damage the brand.

The group has one wholly owned subsidiary, Digisol Systems Limited, and the AR attributes the improved consolidated performance to significantly improved revenue and profitability at Digisol; standalone profit was in turn lifted by the reversal of an earlier impairment on the investment in Digisol amounting to INR 1,288.36 lakhs. Smartlink's own manufacturing revenue also flows substantially through related-party sale of manufactured products to Digisol, so group outcomes concentrate on one brand and one entity. Concentration is compounded by a single manufacturing location (Verna, Goa) and a single R&D centre (Bengaluru).
risks.risk: Dependence on a single wholly owned subsidiary and on a single business line
